s1.plants.parts.prompt: Which part of a plant holds it in the soil and takes in water?
s1.plants.parts.hint: It is the part you cannot usually see.
s1.plants.parts.explain: Roots anchor the plant and take in water from the soil.

s1.plants.parts.prompt: Which part of a plant makes food using sunlight?
s1.plants.parts.hint: They are usually flat and green.
s1.plants.parts.explain: Leaves catch sunlight and use it to make food for the plant.

s1.plants.parts.prompt: Which part holds the plant up and carries water to the leaves?
s1.plants.parts.hint: It is the tall middle part.
s1.plants.parts.explain: The stem holds the plant up and carries water from the roots to the leaves.

s1.plants.parts.prompt: What are the coloured parts of a flower called?
s1.plants.parts.hint: They are often bright to attract insects.
s1.plants.parts.explain: Petals are the coloured parts. They attract insects to the flower.

s1.plants.parts.prompt: What grows into a new plant?
s1.plants.parts.explain: A seed grows into a new plant when it has water, warmth and light.

s1.plants.parts.prompt: Where does a plant get its water from?
choices: from the soil through its roots
from the sky through its petals
from the air through its stem
s1.plants.parts.answer: from the soil through its roots
s1.plants.parts.explain: Roots take in water from the soil.

s1.plants.parts.prompt: Which of these is NOT a part of a flowering plant?
s1.plants.parts.hint: Which one belongs to an animal?
s1.plants.parts.explain: Shells belong to animals like snails, not to plants.

s1.plants.parts.prompt: What is the part of a tree that is like a very thick stem?
s1.plants.parts.hint: You could put your arms around it.
s1.plants.parts.explain: A tree's trunk is a strong, woody stem.

choices: it loses its leaves in autumn
it keeps its leaves all year
s1.plants.trees.answer: it loses its leaves in autumn
s1.plants.trees.hint: Think about bare trees in winter.
s1.plants.trees.explain: Deciduous trees drop their leaves in autumn and grow new ones in spring.

choices: it keeps its leaves all year
it loses its leaves in autumn
it is always green in colour only
s1.plants.trees.answer: it keeps its leaves all year
s1.plants.trees.explain: Evergreen trees keep their leaves all year round.

s1.plants.trees.prompt: Which of these is an evergreen tree?
s1.plants.trees.hint: It has needles instead of flat leaves.
s1.plants.trees.explain: Pine trees are evergreen and have needle-shaped leaves.

s1.plants.trees.hint: You find them in spiky green cases.
s1.plants.trees.explain: Horse chestnut trees drop conkers in spiky cases.

s1.plants.trees.prompt: In which season do deciduous trees lose their leaves?
s1.plants.trees.hint: The leaves turn orange and brown first.
s1.plants.trees.explain: Deciduous trees lose their leaves in autumn.

s1.plants.trees.prompt: Which tree keeps prickly green leaves and red berries in winter?
s1.plants.trees.hint: You see it on Christmas cards.
s1.plants.trees.explain: Holly is evergreen, with prickly leaves and red berries.

s1.plants.trees.prompt: Why do evergreen trees look green in winter?
s1.plants.trees.explain: Evergreens keep their leaves through winter, so they stay green.

s1.animals.groups.hint: They also lay eggs and most can fly.
s1.animals.groups.explain: Birds have feathers, wings and a beak, and they lay eggs.

s1.animals.groups.prompt: Which animal group has scales and lives in water, breathing through gills?
s1.animals.groups.explain: Fish live in water, have scales and fins, and breathe using gills.

s1.animals.groups.prompt: Which animal group has fur or hair and feeds its babies milk?
s1.animals.groups.explain: Mammals have fur or hair and feed their young with milk.

s1.animals.groups.prompt: A frog starts life in water and later lives on land. Which group is it in?
s1.animals.groups.explain: Amphibians such as frogs and newts live in water when young and on land as adults.

s1.animals.groups.prompt: Which group do snakes and lizards belong to?
s1.animals.groups.explain: Reptiles have dry scaly skin and most lay eggs on land.

s1.animals.groups.prompt: Which of these is a mammal?
s1.animals.groups.hint: It lives in the sea but breathes air and feeds its babies milk.
s1.animals.groups.explain: A dolphin is a mammal: it breathes air and feeds its babies milk.

s1.animals.groups.prompt: Which of these is a bird?
s1.animals.groups.explain: A penguin is a bird. It has feathers and lays eggs, even though it cannot fly.

s1.animals.groups.hint: We have hair and babies drink milk.

s1.animals.groups.prompt: Which of these is a reptile?
s1.animals.groups.hint: It has dry scaly skin and a shell.

s1.animals.diets.explain: A carnivore eats meat — other animals.

s1.animals.diets.hint: Think of a cow eating grass.

choices: an animal that eats plants and meat
an animal that eats only meat
an animal that eats only plants
s1.animals.diets.answer: an animal that eats plants and meat
s1.animals.diets.explain: An omnivore eats both plants and meat.

s1.animals.diets.prompt: A rabbit eats grass and vegetables. What is it?
s1.animals.diets.explain: Rabbits eat only plants, so they are herbivores.

s1.animals.diets.prompt: A fox eats small animals, berries and worms. What is it?
s1.animals.diets.hint: It eats more than one kind of food.
s1.animals.diets.explain: Foxes eat both meat and plants, so they are omnivores.
Lions hunt and eat other animals, so they are carnivores.
Giraffes eat leaves from trees, so they are herbivores.

s1.animals.diets.prompt: Why do carnivores often have sharp teeth?
s1.animals.diets.explain: Sharp, pointed teeth help carnivores grip and tear meat.

s1.animals.body-senses.prompt: Which body part do you use to see?
s1.animals.body-senses.hint: You have two of them on your face.
s1.animals.body-senses.explain: You see with your eyes. This sense is called sight.

s1.animals.body-senses.prompt: Which body part do you use to hear?
s1.animals.body-senses.hint: One on each side of your head.
s1.animals.body-senses.explain: You hear with your ears. This sense is called hearing.

s1.animals.body-senses.prompt: Which body part do you use to smell?
s1.animals.body-senses.hint: It is in the middle of your face.

s1.animals.body-senses.prompt: Which body part do you use to taste?
Which sense do you use to feel whether something is soft?
s1.animals.body-senses.hint: You mostly use your hands and skin.
s1.animals.body-senses.explain: Touch lets you feel textures with your skin.

s1.animals.body-senses.prompt: How many senses do humans have?
s1.animals.body-senses.hint: Sight, hearing, smell, taste and one more.
s1.animals.body-senses.explain: The five senses are sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch.

s1.animals.body-senses.prompt: Which body part joins your hand to your arm?
s1.animals.body-senses.hint: You might wear a watch there.
s1.animals.body-senses.explain: The wrist joins the hand to the arm.

s1.animals.body-senses.prompt: Which body part bends in the middle of your leg?
s1.animals.body-senses.hint: You bend it to sit down.
s1.animals.body-senses.explain: The knee is the joint in the middle of your leg.

s1.mat.identify.prompt: What material is a window usually made from?
s1.mat.identify.explain: Windows are made of glass because it is transparent.

s1.mat.identify.prompt: What material is a woolly jumper made from?
s1.mat.identify.explain: Woolly jumpers are made from wool, which comes from sheep.

s1.mat.identify.prompt: What material is a spoon usually made from?
s1.mat.identify.explain: Most spoons are made of metal because it is strong and easy to clean.

s1.mat.identify.prompt: What material is a book's pages made from?
s1.mat.identify.explain: Pages are made of paper, which comes from wood.

s1.mat.identify.prompt: What is the difference between an object and a material?
choices: the object is the thing, the material is what it is made of
s1.mat.identify.answer: the object is the thing, the material is what it is made of
s1.mat.identify.hint: A chair is an object. Wood is a material.
s1.mat.identify.explain: An object is a thing; a material is what that thing is made from.

s1.mat.identify.prompt: What material is a car tyre made from?
s1.mat.identify.explain: Tyres are made from rubber because it grips the road and bends.

s1.mat.identify.prompt: What material is a wall of a house often made from?
s1.mat.identify.hint: It is hard and stacked in rows.
s1.mat.identify.explain: Walls are often made from brick because it is strong.

s1.mat.identify.prompt: Which object is made of wood?
s1.mat.identify.hint: Think about what is around the pencil lead.
s1.mat.identify.explain: Pencils are usually made of wood.

s1.mat.properties.prompt: Which word describes something you can see through?
s1.mat.properties.explain: Transparent means you can see through it.

s1.mat.properties.prompt: Which word describes something you cannot see through at all?
s1.mat.properties.explain: Opaque means light cannot pass through it.

s1.mat.properties.hint: You can pull it and it springs back.
s1.mat.properties.explain: Elastic bands are stretchy — they change shape and spring back.

s1.mat.properties.hint: Which one keeps you dry in the rain?
s1.mat.properties.explain: Plastic is waterproof, so water cannot soak through.

s1.mat.properties.prompt: Which material is absorbent (soaks up water)?
s1.mat.properties.hint: Which one would you use to mop up a spill?
s1.mat.properties.explain: Paper towels are absorbent, so they soak up water.

s1.mat.properties.hint: Which one is difficult to squash?
s1.mat.properties.explain: Rock is very hard — it does not squash or bend easily.

s1.mat.properties.hint: Which one can you curl up?
s1.mat.properties.explain: A rubber hose is flexible, so it bends without breaking.

s1.seasons.changes.prompt: How many seasons are there in a year?
s1.seasons.changes.hint: Spring, summer, autumn and one more.
s1.seasons.changes.explain: The four seasons are spring, summer, autumn and winter.

s1.seasons.changes.prompt: In which season do many baby animals get born and buds open?
s1.seasons.changes.explain: Spring is when many plants start growing and baby animals are born.

s1.seasons.changes.prompt: Which season has the longest days and the most sunshine?
s1.seasons.changes.hint: You might go on holiday and it stays light late.
s1.seasons.changes.explain: In summer the days are longest and it is warmest.

s1.seasons.changes.prompt: In which season do leaves turn orange and fall?
s1.seasons.changes.explain: In autumn deciduous leaves change colour and drop.

s1.seasons.changes.prompt: Which season is the coldest with the shortest days?
s1.seasons.changes.explain: Winter is coldest and has the shortest days.
The order is spring, summer, autumn, winter.

s1.seasons.changes.prompt: Why should you never look straight at the Sun?
s1.seasons.changes.explain: The Sun is so bright it can permanently damage your eyes.

s1.seasons.changes.prompt: What kind of weather is most common in winter in the UK?
s1.seasons.changes.hint: Think about what you wear in December.
s1.seasons.changes.explain: UK winters are usually cold and wet, with some frost and snow.
